mainTopic: One sandal for a wounded foot, the order of putting on shoes, and going out on שבת with תפילין and amulets
overview: The גמרא infers that a person with a wounded foot may go out on שבת in one sandal. רב הונא and חייא בר רב disagree about which foot gets it, and a proof from a story about רבי יוחנן is rejected because it fits both views. This leads to רבי יוחנן's rule that the left shoe goes on first, like תפילין, which clashes with a ברייתא that says right first. רב יוסף allows both orders, אביי objects, and a ירא שמים like מר בריה דרבנא arranges things to satisfy both, while רב כהנא was not particular. The גמרא then quotes the full ברייתא: right first for putting on shoes, washing and oiling, left first for taking shoes off, and the head first when oiling the whole body. Next, רב ספרא explains the משנה's rule about going out with תפילין, in two versions, and concludes that תפילין are worn like a garment. Finally, רב פפא explains that an amulet is allowed if its writer is an expert, and a ברייתא defines a proven amulet and allows tying it on even in רשות הרבים, with a condition that finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: Inference: someone with a wound may go out in one sandal
steps.stepSummary: From the earlier rule against going out in one sandal, the גמרא infers that if a person has a wound on his foot, he may go out with one sandal.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if he has a wound on his foot, he may go out with one sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the earlier rule in reverse: if the ban applies only when there is no wound, then a person with a wound is allowed one sandal. This sets up the next question about which foot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general worry is that people seeing someone in one sandal will suspect he is carrying the other one. A wound explains why he wears only one, so the worry falls away.

phrases.english: This implies: if there is a wound on his foot, he may go out (with one sandal).
phrases.notes: This comes from the ruling just before: you can't go out in one sandal unless you have a wound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of going out in a single sandal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person with a foot wound may go out on שבת wearing one sandal.

steps.title: Which foot wears the sandal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which foot gets the single sandal: the wounded one or the healthy one.
steps.simpleTranslation: On which of his feet does he go out with the sandal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question: if he may wear one sandal, which foot does it go on? This sets up two opposing answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real request for information, not an attack. The answer depends on why people wear sandals in the first place.

phrases.english: With which of them (which foot) does he go out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a detail about the permission stated in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the single sandal goes on the wounded foot or on the healthy foot.

steps.title: רב הונא: on the wounded foot, because a sandal prevents pain
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the sandal goes on the wounded foot. This shows he holds that a sandal is worn to prevent pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: on the foot that has the wound. So he apparently holds that a sandal is made to prevent pain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers that the sandal goes on the wounded foot. The גמרא then explains his reasoning: sandals are for avoiding pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If sandals exist to prevent pain, a person walking with one bare foot clearly does not mind the pain on that foot. People will understand that the one sandal is only there to protect the wound, so nobody will suspect he is carrying the other sandal.

keyTerms.meaning: For the purpose of preventing pain

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
On the one (foot) that has a wound.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר, סַנְדָּל לְשׁוּם צַעַר עֲבִיד.
phrases.english: Apparently he holds: a sandal is made to prevent pain.
phrases.notes: The reasoning is the גמרא's own explanation of רב הונא's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּאוֹתָהּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ מַכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sandal goes on the wounded foot, since a sandal's purpose is to prevent pain.

steps.title: חייא בר רב: on the healthy foot, because a sandal gives comfort
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב says the sandal goes on the healthy foot, since sandals are for comfort. The visible wound on the bare foot explains why it has no sandal.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב said: on the foot without the wound. So he apparently holds that a sandal is made for comfort. And the foot that has the wound, its wound shows why it is bare.
steps.whatsHappening: חייא בר רב gives the opposite answer: the sandal goes on the healthy foot. The גמרא explains that he sees sandals as a comfort item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If sandals are for comfort, a person naturally wants one on his healthy foot. People will not suspect he is carrying the other sandal, because they can see the wound on the bare foot and understand he cannot wear a sandal there.

keyTerms.meaning: For the purpose of comfort / pleasure

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that only one sandal is worn and that onlookers must not suspect carrying. They disagree only about which foot, and that depends on what a sandal is for.

phrases.english: And Chiyya bar Rav said:
On the one (foot) that does not have a wound.
Apparently he holds: it (a sandal) is made for comfort,
and this one (foot) that has a wound —
its wound testifies about it (why it has no sandal).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב אָמַר בְּאוֹתָהּ שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ מַכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing answer to the same question that רב הונא answered.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sandal goes on the healthy foot, since a sandal's purpose is comfort, and the wound explains the bare foot.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: the wounded foot, because a sandal is for pain (צער). חייא בר רב: the healthy foot, because a sandal is for comfort (תענוג).

steps.title: Proof that רבי יוחנן agrees with רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story to show that רבי יוחנן agrees with רב הונא. When his attendant handed him his right sandal first, רבי יוחנן said, 'You have made it a wound.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן also agrees with רב הונא. For רבי יוחנן said to רב שמן בר אבא: 'Give me my sandals.' He gave him the right one. רבי יוחנן said: 'You have made it a wound.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove from a story that רבי יוחנן sides with רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's custom was to put on the left shoe first, so receiving the right one first meant he would end up wearing only the right shoe. By saying 'you made it a wound,' he seems to mean the right foot, the one with the shoe, now looks wounded. That would match רב הונא, who says the shoe goes on the wounded foot.

keyTerms.meaning: You have made it (into) a wound

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן was not actually wounded. His point was that, because of his custom of putting on the left shoe first, he now had to walk around in one shoe like a wounded person.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סָבַר לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan also holds like this view of Rav Huna.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Yochanan said to Rav Shemen bar Abba:
Give me my sandals.
He gave him the right one.
He said to him: You have made it (the right foot) a wound.
phrases.notes: Read this way, the shod right foot is treated as the 'wounded' one, which matches רב הונא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סָבַר לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to decide between the two opinions by showing that רבי יוחנן supports רב הונא.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's view that the single sandal goes on the wounded foot.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי יוחנן and רב שמן בר אבא handing him the right sandal.

steps.title: Rejection: the story also fits חייא בר רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Perhaps רבי יוחנן agrees with חייא בר רב and meant that the bare left foot now looks wounded.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he holds like חייא בר רב, and this is what he meant: 'You have made the left foot a wound.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by reading רבי יוחנן's words a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'You made it a wound' could refer to the bare left foot, not the shod right foot. If the bare foot looks like the wounded one, that matches חייא בר רב, who puts the shoe on the healthy foot. So the story proves nothing either way, and the dispute stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what he meant

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from רבי יוחנן fails because his words can be read to fit either opinion. The dispute between רב הונא and חייא בר רב remains unresolved.

phrases.aramaic: וְדִילְמָא כְּחִיָּיא בַּר רַב סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: But perhaps he holds like Chiyya bar Rav,
and this is what he was saying:
You have made the left (foot) a wound.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא כְּחִיָּיא בַּר רַב סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the story. Neither opinion is refuted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'you made it a wound' is ambiguous. It could refer to the bare left foot, which fits חייא בר רב.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן holds that shoes, like tefillin, start on the left
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the background of רבי יוחנן's story. He holds that the left shoe goes on first, just like תפילין go on the left arm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning. רבי יוחנן said: shoes are like תפילין. Just as תפילין go on the left, shoes also start on the left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why רבי יוחנן was upset when he was handed the right sandal first. He holds that the left shoe should go on first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line explains the background of the story in steps 5-6. רבי יוחנן holds that shoes follow תפילין, so the left shoe must go on first. Once the attendant handed him the right sandal, he could no longer put on the left one, and he had to go out in one shoe like a wounded person. This background fits both readings of 'you made it a wound.' It does not decide between רב הונא and חייא בר רב.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning (this fits his known opinion)
תפילין, worn on the left arm

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning.
For Rabbi Yochanan said:
As with tefillin, so with shoes.
Just as tefillin are on the left,
so too shoes begin with the left.
phrases.notes: The left shoe is put on first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the background of the story in steps 5-6: רבי יוחנן's known rule that the left shoe goes on first is why being handed the right shoe left him in one shoe.
steps.raayaObject: That the incident in step 5 fits רבי יוחנן's known view that the left shoe must go on first
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's own statement comparing shoes to תפילין

steps.title: A ברייתא says the right shoe goes on first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא that says to put on the right shoe first.
steps.simpleTranslation: An objection was raised: when a person puts on shoes, he puts on the right one first and then the left one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's rule with a ברייתא that teaches the opposite order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said left first. The ברייתא clearly says right first, then left. A teaching from the time of the תנאים carries great weight, so this is a serious challenge to an אמורא.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
When he puts on shoes, he puts on the right one
and afterward puts on the left one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of רבי יוחנן quoted in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that the left shoe goes on first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly rules right first, which contradicts an אמורא's ruling.

steps.title: רב יוסף: either way is acceptable
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that since a ברייתא supports one order and רבי יוחנן supports the other, a person may follow either one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: now that a ברייתא teaches this, and רבי יוחנן said that, whoever does it this way has done properly, and whoever does it that way has done properly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף settles the clash by saying that both practices are acceptable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף does not choose a winner. Each order has a respected source behind it, so he allows both: right first like the ברייתא, or left first like רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that it was taught this way
One who did it this way did properly

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Now that it was taught this way (right first),
and Rabbi Yochanan said that way (left first),
one who did it this way did properly,
and one who did it that way did properly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף הַשְׁתָּא דְּתַנְיָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the contradiction in Step 8 by allowing both practices.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא disproves רבי יוחנן, so only right first is correct.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both orders have support, so either practice is acceptable.

steps.title: אביי: perhaps רבי יוחנן never heard the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. Maybe רבי יוחנן never heard the ברייתא, and if he had, he would have taken back his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: perhaps רבי יוחנן had not heard this teaching, and if he had heard it, he would have retracted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי argues against treating the two sources as equal. רבי יוחנן's view may simply have come from not knowing the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed that רבי יוחנן knowingly disagreed. אביי points out that if רבי יוחנן was unaware of the ברייתא, his opinion carries no real weight against it. Then only right first would be correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means the ברייתא just quoted, a תנאי teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Here מַתְנִיתִין does not mean our משנה. It refers to the ברייתא quoted in Step 8.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Perhaps Rabbi Yochanan, this teaching,
had not heard it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי הֲוָה שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ הֲוָה הָדַר בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: and had he heard it, he would have retracted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's conclusion that both practices are valid.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יוסף's assumption that רבי יוחנן's view stands equal to the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן may not have known the ברייתא, so his opinion may not be a deliberate disagreement.

steps.title: אביי: or he heard it and held the הלכה does not follow it
steps.stepSummary: אביי offers a second possibility: רבי יוחנן did hear the ברייתא but held that the הלכה does not follow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else he did hear it, and he held that the הלכה is not like that teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives another reason why both practices cannot be equally right. רבי יוחנן may have consciously rejected the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case רבי יוחנן's disagreement is a decision that the הלכה does not follow the ברייתא. Either way, one view must be the הלכה, so you cannot simply say both are fine.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה does not follow that teaching

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says left shoe first, like תפילין. A ברייתא says right first. רב יוסף allowed both. אביי objected that in either case, whether רבי יוחנן never heard it or rejected it, there must be one correct הלכה.

phrases.english: Or alternatively, he did hear it,
and he held that the halacha is not in accordance with that teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative reason for rejecting רב יוסף's 'both are fine' position.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יוסף's conclusion that either practice is acceptable
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If רבי יוחנן knowingly ruled against the ברייתא, it is a real dispute that needs a single ruling, not a choice of either.

steps.title: A God-fearing person satisfies both views
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rules that a ירא שמים should find a way to fulfill both the ברייתא (right shoe first) and רבי יוחנן (left shoe first).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: A person who fears Heaven fulfills both opinions.
steps.whatsHappening: After the back-and-forth about which shoe goes first, רב נחמן בר יצחק offers a practical way out: a truly careful person does both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said a person may pick either opinion. אביי then objected that one opinion must be the הלכה, either the ברייתא or רבי יוחנן. רב נחמן בר יצחק avoids picking a side: an extra-careful person arranges things so both opinions are satisfied.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who fears Heaven, someone extra careful in serving הקב״ה
Both of them, here meaning both opinions

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
One who fears Heaven fulfills both opinions.
phrases.notes: Both means the ברייתא (right first) and רבי יוחנן (left first).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the uncertainty that אביי raised by offering a way to satisfy both opinions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An extra-careful person should satisfy both the right-first and left-first opinions.

steps.title: Who acted this way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who this ירא שמים was and answers: מר בריה דרבנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is this person? מר בריה דרבנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names a real person who followed this careful practice. This sets up the next step, which explains exactly what he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming a specific אמורא shows that this was an actual practice and not just a theory. The name prepares us for the practical description that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Mar, son of Rabbana, an אמורא

phrases.english: And who is this?
Mar, son of Rabbana.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the ירא שמים mentioned in step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the God-fearing person who satisfies both opinions?

steps.title: How he fulfilled both opinions
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבנא put on the right shoe first without tying it, then put on and tied the left, and only then tied the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did he do it? He put on his right shoe and did not tie it. Then he put on his left shoe and tied it. Then he went back and tied the right one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the exact method. Putting on the right shoe first satisfies the ברייתא, and tying the left shoe first satisfies רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trick is to split the act into two parts: putting the shoe on and tying it. The right foot gets the first putting-on, and the left foot gets the first tying. Since רבי יוחנן compared shoes to תפילין, which are tied on the left, the tying is the part that counts for his view.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate actions here: putting on and tying. The right shoe goes on first, but the left shoe is tied first. Do not mix up which foot gets which 'first.'

phrases.english: How does he do it?
He puts on his right shoe and does not tie it,
and he puts on his left shoe and ties it,
and then he goes back and ties the right one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the practical method of the person named in step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly did he do to satisfy both opinions?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Right shoe on first but left unfastened, then left shoe on and tied, then the right tied.

steps.title: רב כהנא was not particular about the order
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי testifies that he saw רב כהנא pay no attention to which shoe went first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I saw that רב כהנא was not particular about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a report about a different practice: רב כהנא did not care which shoe came first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the whole question of shoe order was a matter of good practice and not a strict requirement. A great אמורא like רב כהנא did not insist on any order at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Was not particular, did not insist

steps.whatToRemember: On shoe order: the ברייתא says right first, רבי יוחנן says left first, a ירא שמים does both (right on first, left tied first), and רב כהנא was not particular.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I saw that Rav Kahana was not particular.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a more relaxed practice next to the careful one in steps 12-14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא did not insist on any shoe order.

steps.title: The full ברייתא: right shoe on first, left shoe off first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the full ברייתא: put on the right shoe first, and take off the left shoe first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When he puts on shoes, he puts on the right one and afterward the left one. When he takes them off, he takes off the left one and afterward the right one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the whole ברייתא that was cited earlier in shortened form, starting with putting shoes on and taking them off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right side is given honor, so it goes first when putting on. When taking off, the order flips so that the right foot stays covered longer. Both rules come from the same idea: the right side gets priority.
steps.confusionAlert: Taking off is not 'right first' as well. The left comes off first so the right shoe stays on longer. That is still honoring the right side.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
When he puts on shoes,
he puts on the right one
and afterward puts on the left one.
When he takes them off,
he takes off the left one
and afterward takes off the right one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes in full the ברייתא that was cited briefly in step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Right shoe on first; left shoe off first.

steps.title: Washing and oiling: right first, and the head first for the whole body
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: wash and oil the right side first, and when oiling the whole body, start with the head because it is king over all the limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he washes, he washes the right and afterward the left. When he oils, he oils the right and afterward the left. And one who wants to oil his whole body oils his head first, because it is king over all his limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies the same right-first rule to washing and oiling. It adds that the head comes first when oiling the entire body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each body care action follows an order of importance. Between the two sides, the right comes first. For the whole body, the head comes first because it is the most important part, like a king over the other limbs.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's principle: the more important part goes first. Right before left for shoes, washing, and oiling, and the head first for the whole body.

phrases.english: When he washes,
he washes the right
and afterward washes the left.
When he spreads oil,
he oils the right
and afterward the left.
And one who wants to oil his whole body
oils his head first,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מֶלֶךְ עַל כׇּל אֵיבָרָיו.
phrases.english: because it is king over all his limbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with more cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wash and oil the right side first; when oiling the whole body, oil the head first.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: not with תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's next phrase: a man may not go out on שבת wearing תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not with תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the next item, setting up רב ספרא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic. The משנה lists things a man may not go out with on שבת, and תפילין is one of them. The quote prepares for the question of why this is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: And not with תפילין (quote from the משנה)

phrases.english: And not with phylacteries.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, introducing a new discussion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the shoe discussion and returns to the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not go out on שבת with תפילין.

steps.title: The ban applies even if שבת is a time for תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא explains that the ban is not only according to the view that תפילין are not worn on שבת. Even those who hold they are worn agree, because one might come to carry them in a רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: Do not say this follows only the one who says שבת is not a time for תפילין. Rather, even according to the one who says שבת is a time for תפילין, he may not go out with them, because he might come to carry them in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא tells us the reason behind the משנה's rule and shows that it works for both opinions about wearing תפילין on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought the משנה only follows the view that תפילין do not belong on שבת, so they would count as a burden. רב ספרא says no. Even if תפילין are proper to wear on שבת, there is a separate worry: he might take them off and carry them in his hand in a רשות הרבים, which is forbidden by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
A time when תפילין are worn
Perhaps he will come to carry

steps.confusionAlert: רב ספרא is not saying תפילין are a forbidden burden. He is saying that even if wearing them is fine, the חכמים worried he might end up carrying them in his hand.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the משנה work for both sides of the debate about תפילין on שבת. It rests the rule on a protective גזירה against carrying.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
Do not say this is according to the one who says
Shabbat is not a time for phylacteries.
Rather, even according to the one who says
Shabbat is a time for phylacteries,
he may not go out with them,
lest he come to carry them in the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the משנה's rule quoted in step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even if שבת is a time for תפילין, one may not go out with them, because he might come to carry them in a רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Second version: רב ספרא explains why there is no sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: Some people link רב ספרא's statement to the end of the משנה instead. Going out with תפילין does not make a person bring a חטאת, even for the view that שבת is not a time for תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach רב ספרא's statement on the last part of the משנה: 'If he went out, he does not bring a חטאת.' רב ספרא said: Don't think this is only for the view that שבת is a time for תפילין. Even for the view that שבת is not a time for תפילין, he does not bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב ספרא's words. In this version he is explaining a different part of the משנה: the rule that a person who went out with תפילין does not bring a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שבת is a time for תפילין, it is easy to see why there is no חטאת: he is simply wearing them. But if שבת is not a time for תפילין, you might think they become a plain object he is carrying, which would require a חטאת. רב ספרא says that even on that view, there is still no חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it (a second version of a statement)
The latter (end) part of a משנה
Sin-offering, brought for an accidental Torah-level sin
A time when one is supposed to wear תפילין

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first version (step 19), רב ספרא explained the opening ban: 'don't go out with תפילין,' because one might carry them. In this second version, he explains the end rule: 'no חטאת if he did go out.'

phrases.english: And some teach it on the latter clause:
'And if he went out, he is not liable to bring a sin-offering.'
Rav Safra said:
Do not say this is only according to the one who said
Shabbat is a time for tefillin;
rather, even according to the one who said
Shabbat is not a time for tefillin,
he is not liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of step 19: the same speaker's statement, applied to the end of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no חטאת for going out with תפילין on שבת, even for the view that שבת is not a time for תפילין.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why there is no חטאת even for the view that שבת is not a time for תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב ספרא's ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is sharp because, on this view, the תפילין are not being worn for the מצוה on שבת. So why isn't wearing them counted as carrying an object?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why going out with תפילין does not require a חטאת, even if שבת is not a time for תפילין.

steps.title: Tefillin are worn like clothing
steps.stepSummary: The answer: תפילין are worn the way clothing is worn, so this is not carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is done in the manner of wearing clothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that תפילין are worn on the body like clothing. So going out with them is not the Torah-level kind of carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying on שבת means transporting an object. Something worn on the body the normal way is not 'carried.' Even if there is no מצוה to wear תפילין on שבת, they are still worn like a garment, so there is no חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: In the manner of wearing a garment

steps.whatToRemember: In this second version, the reason there is no חטאת for going out with תפילין is simple: they are worn like clothing, not carried like an object.
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the basic rule of carrying on שבת: things worn on the body in the normal way are not a burden being carried.

phrases.english: It is done in the manner of a garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תפילין are worn like a garment, so wearing them outside is not Torah-level carrying.

steps.title: The משנה's next phrase: an amulet not from an expert
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה: a man may not go out with an amulet that is not from an expert.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And not with an amulet when it is not from an expert.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next phrase of the משנה, about going out on שבת with a קמיע. This sets up רב פפא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קמיע that really works counts like something worn for the body's benefit, so one may go out with it. One that is not 'from an expert' is just an object being carried. The question now is what 'expert' means.

keyTerms.meaning: Amulet: a written charm or bundle of herbs worn for healing or protection

phrases.english: And not with an amulet
when it is not from an expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא בְּקָמֵיעַ בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִן הַמּוּמְחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of תפילין and returns to the משנה's list for its next item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not go out on שבת with a קמיע that is not from an expert.

steps.title: רב פפא: an expert writer is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that if the person who wrote the amulet is an expert, one may go out with it. The amulet itself does not need to be proven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Don't think you need both an expert writer and a proven amulet. Once the writer is an expert, it is allowed, even if the amulet itself has not been proven.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defines the משנה's word 'expert.' It refers to the person who wrote the amulet, not to the amulet itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could have read the משנה as needing two conditions: an expert writer and an amulet that has already worked. רב פפא removes the second condition. The writer's skill alone makes the amulet trustworthy enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The man (here, the person who wrote the amulet)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Do not say it is only allowed when the man is an expert
and the amulet is proven;
rather, once the man is an expert,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מוּמְחֶה קָמֵיעַ.
phrases.english: even though the amulet is not proven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא תֵּימָא עַד דְּמוּמְחֶה גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה phrase quoted in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An expert writer is enough. The amulet does not need its own proven track record.

steps.title: The משנה's wording supports רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'from an expert,' pointing to a person, not 'not proven,' which would describe the amulet. This supports רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is exact too. The משנה says 'when it is not from an expert.' It does not say 'when it is not proven.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רב פפא right from the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From the expert' (מן המומחה) describes where the amulet came from: a person. If the משנה had wanted the amulet itself to be proven, it would have said 'when it is not proven' (שאינו מומחה). The wording it chose focuses on the writer.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact (it supports this)
Learn from it (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: In the משנה, 'expert' means the person who wrote the amulet. This is shown by the words 'מִן הַמּוּמְחֶה,' which mean 'from the expert.'

phrases.english: It is also precise, for it teaches:
'And not with an amulet when it is not from an expert,'
and it does not teach:
'when it is not proven.'
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's reading from step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's view that an expert writer is enough.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'מִן הַמּוּמְחֶה' (from the expert), rather than 'שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּמְחֶה' (not proven).

steps.title: What makes an amulet proven: three healings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines a proven amulet: one that healed, healed again, and healed a third time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: What is a proven amulet? Any amulet that healed, then healed again, then healed a third time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that defines when an amulet counts as proven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An amulet becomes proven by working three times. Three successes show it is reliable and not just luck.

keyTerms.meaning: Healed, did it a second time, and a third time

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this contradicts רב פפא. He said an expert writer is enough to go out with an amulet. This ברייתא simply defines what a proven amulet is.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
What is a proven amulet?
Any that healed, and did so again, and a third time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that defines the idea of a 'proven amulet' from steps 23-25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An amulet is proven once it has healed three times.

steps.title: The rule applies to every kind of amulet and illness
steps.stepSummary: The three-healings rule applies to written amulets and herbal ones, and to serious and non-serious illnesses alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is true for a written amulet and for an amulet made of roots. It is true for a sick person in danger and for a sick person not in danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and tells us how widely the three-healings rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists two pairs to show there is no difference. The type of amulet (written or herbs) does not matter. The type of illness (dangerous or not) does not matter. The same standard applies everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: A sick person whose life is in danger

steps.whatToRemember: A proven amulet is one that healed three times. This standard is the same for written and herbal amulets, and for dangerous and non-dangerous illnesses.

phrases.english: Both a written amulet
and an amulet of roots;
both a sick person who is in danger
and a sick person who is not in danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד קָמֵיעַ שֶׁל כְּתָב וְאֶחָד קָמֵיעַ שֶׁל עִיקָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 26 and spells out how widely its rule applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three-healings rule applies to written and herbal amulets, and to dangerous and non-dangerous illnesses alike.

steps.title: A proven amulet may also be worn as prevention
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the amulet is allowed even for someone who never had the illness and wears it so that he will not get sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not only for someone who already fell from epilepsy. It is also for someone who wears it so that he will not fall.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and makes the permission wider: the amulet is allowed even for prevention, not only for someone already sick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think an amulet counts as something you wear (and not something you carry) only when it treats an existing illness. The ברייתא says no. Protecting a healthy person also counts as a real use of the amulet, so he may go out with it on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: one who has fallen from epilepsy (already has the illness)
will fall from epilepsy (future, the thing he wants to prevent)
not only ... but also (a phrase that widens the rule)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'לא שנכפה' as 'not for someone who already fell.' It means 'not ONLY for someone who already fell.' The phrase adds a case. It does not take one away.

phrases.english: Not only one who has already fallen (from epilepsy),
phrases.notes: This is someone already sick, wearing it to stop another attack.

phrases.english: but even so that he will not fall.
phrases.notes: This is a healthy person wearing it just as protection.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא. Step 27 widened the rule to all kinds of amulets and illnesses. This step widens it to prevention as well as treatment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A proven amulet may be worn on שבת even by a healthy person who wears it only to protect himself.

steps.title: Tying and untying the amulet in the public domain
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא allows tying the amulet on and untying it even in רשות הרבים, and then begins a condition that limits this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he may tie it and untie it even in the public domain, as long as he does not tie it...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a practical rule: you may put the amulet on or take it off even while in רשות הרבים. It then begins a condition ('as long as he does not tie it...'), which is finished on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the amulet counts as something worn, handling it in רשות הרבים is not treated as carrying. Tying it on or untying it there is fine. The word ובלבד tells us a limit is coming on how it may be tied. The details of that limit appear in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: the public domain, where carrying on שבת is forbidden
provided that; as long as (introduces a condition)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the amulet is fully treated as clothing or jewelry. It is not just allowed to stay on the body; it may even be put on and taken off in public.

phrases.english: And he may tie and untie it
phrases.notes: Putting the amulet on and taking it off.

phrases.english: even in the public domain.
phrases.notes: 'Even' shows this is the strongest case, where carrying would normally be forbidden.

phrases.english: as long as he does not tie it
phrases.notes: The condition starts here and is finished on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא moves on from who may wear the amulet (step 28) to how it may be handled in רשות הרבים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may tie on and untie a proven amulet even in רשות הרבים, subject to a condition about how it is tied.
